one_month_reasoning: Inside Oct 2-31: (1) a September production update is still likely mid-October (only the infrastructure section moved to quarterly), expected ~80 EH/s self-mining: mostly known, low impact. (2) BTC (~$84.8k) and hashprice (~$39/PH/day) dominate a high-beta miner. (3) Possible Tydal project-financing terms: none had been announced as of 10/2 (search found only the August release saying leading institutions are engaged). Non-dilutive project debt priced near the TeraWulf/Cipher 7.1-7.75% secured-note precedents would be +; an ATM-heavy or convert raise would be -. Q3 results (~Nov 9-18), A201/A102 revenue starts and any A202 offtake fall outside the window. Round 4 changes long-dated value only (site coverage, split discount rate, net-debt bridge); nothing in October depends on it, so the 1-month ladder stays near-symmetric around $10.6 at ~30% monthly vol with a slight downward median tilt for financing/dilution headlines, unchanged from round 3.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site DCF at split discount rates ($-2.02; contracted cash flows at 8.75% LC-backed / 10.5% unrated, everything else at 12% WACC; $-2.43 at a single 12%) at 35% and a SOTP ($6.47: Tydal $1.69B, AI cloud $1.23B, Tydal P3 $0.12B, powered-land option $0.72B, mining $0.75B, less corporate G&A $0.35B and $2.38B horizon net debt, 275M shares) at 65% = $3.50. The 2032 notes are held as debt and no ATM issuance is credited.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site unlevered DCF valued at 2027-10-01, model years Oct-27..Sep-42 plus terminal at g 2%; every inventory site appears once (see site_coverage). Discounting split: Tydal lease years 1-5 (covered by the ~$1.3B JPM-arranged LCs) at 8.75%; Tydal lease years 6-10 (Volta credit only) and the A101/A102/A201 offtakes (undisclosed, unrated customers, >50% capex prepaid) at 10.5%; Tydal years 11-16 (after the no-fee walk right), post-contract tails, refreshes, all pipeline (A202, Knoxville, Wenatchee, Tydal P3, US HPC options), mining, corporate and terminal at 12% WACC. Site PVs ($M, split rate): Tydal 1,694; A201 832; A102 238; A101 38; legacy fleet 38; Knoxville 189 (35% x 55 MW); Wenatchee 34; A202 -144 (45% offtake, 10-yr facility fee paid regardless); Tydal P3 123 (40%); Rockdale HPC option 65 (25%, net of lost mining); Weathersfield 33 (15%); Clarington 24 (10%); Molde AI option 23 (10%); mining 307 across six sites; Massillon 47 MW rebuild -18; Fox Creek, Gelephu, Sparks 0; corporate -2,139; tax shield/NOL +486. EV $1,824M (single-rate $1,713M), less $2,380M horizon net debt, / 275M = -$2.02 (single -$2.43). Round-4 changes: A202 rebuilt as uncontracted GPU cloud that Bitdeer pays a 10-yr facility fee for; A201 at 85% on the signed >70% ($340M/yr) and spot path for the rest; capex multiple 1.6x first-year revenue for GB300 halls ($28M/MW for Vera Rubin-era builds), refresh at 75% of today's per-MW price (about NPV-zero); 2032 notes as debt and no ATM; horizon capex bridge fixed (A201, A102 balance, mining, Knoxville/Wenatchee shells now in net debt); Knoxville, Wenatchee, Tydal P3, Rockdale/Weathersfield/Clarington/Molde options added; prepayments counted once (cash in before or at capex, then deducted from contract revenue over the term). Sensitivities (split rate): life 5y -$2.43, 7y -$1.76; supply-long steeper path -$2.54; WACC 11% -$1.75, 13% -$2.26. Limited liability: a negative DCF means cash flows do not cover ~$2.4B of debt at the horizon; equity value then rests on option value (SOTP market legs, BTC, new leases).

inputs_detail.input: Contracted discount rate, LC-backed (Tydal lease years 1-5)
inputs_detail.derivation: Bitdeer has no secured debt priced against a contract (inventory contracts_credit: its only secured priced debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0%, against mining rigs and generic assets). Nearest precedent: HPC-lease project notes backed by an investment-grade backstop: TeraWulf $3.2B 7.75% (Oct-2025, BB) and Cipher $1.4B 7.125% (Nov-2025). They were issued when the 10-yr Treasury was ~4.0-4.1% (judgment, from memory of the period), a ~3.4pp spread. 5.29% + 3.4pp = ~8.7%. The ~$1.3B of JPM-arranged LCs covers about the first 5 lease years of rent (sum ~$1.24B). I round to 8.75% because the LCs are only 'anticipated' and the build still carries completion risk.

inputs_detail.input: Contracted discount rate, unrated (Tydal lease years 6-10; A101/A102/A201 offtakes)
inputs_detail.derivation: Volta is a private 2026-founded developer with no rating, and its reported end-customer deal (~6 yrs) ends before Tydal's year 10. The GPU-cloud customers are undisclosed. Prepayments covering >50% of capex cut loss-given-default, and the terms are short (5 yrs). So the rate sits between 8.75% and the 12% WACC, slightly nearer the WACC.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: At Oct-2027: Tydal $1.69B (split-rate site value; LC conditionality in the 8.75% rate) + AI cloud $1.23B (A201 $0.83B, A102 $0.24B, A101 $0.04B, legacy $0.04B, Knoxville $0.19B, Wenatchee $0.03B, A202 -$0.14B including the facility fee) + Tydal P3 $0.12B + powered-land option $0.72B (821 energized convertible MW at Rockdale/Massillon/Molde x $0.6M + 1,150 pipeline MW at Rockdale +179, Weathersfield, Clarington and Fox Creek x $0.2M; Knoxville/Wenatchee now valued as AI cloud, not land) + mining $0.75B (2.2x ~$345M) - corporate G&A $0.35B (new: ~$118M/yr x 3) = EV $4.16B; less $2.38B net debt; / 275M = $6.47.

inputs_detail.derivation: Same cash flows as round 3 (Apr-27 start, 90% NOI less 3% capex, year-7 default overlay, 25% year-10 walk, 50% renewal value after year 16), now discounted 8.75% / 10.5% / 12% by contract slice instead of a flat 10.5% with a separate x0.9 LC haircut. Remaining ~$500M capex sits in net debt.

Site DCF values (split rate). A201 rises because its GB300 capex now sits in horizon net debt and the committed 70% is weighted 85% at $340M/yr. A202 flips from +$0.25B (colocation income) to -$0.14B (fee paid, 45% offtake). Knoxville and Wenatchee are added at 35%.

Each MW counted once. Energized mining MW that could convert (Rockdale 563, Massillon 174, Molde 84) at $0.6M/MW above mining value, i.e. ~7% of contracted value (CoinShares). Pipeline MW not yet energized (Rockdale +179, Weathersfield 300, Clarington 570 in litigation, Fox Creek 101) at $0.2M/MW. Bhutan, Ethiopia (mining only) and Gelephu (non-binding LOI) get none. Tydal, Knoxville and Wenatchee are excluded because they are valued elsewhere.

$1.15B mining revenue x 30% margin; 2.2x (down from 2.5x) because the Apr-2028 halving lands 6 months after the valuation date; CoinShares miners without AI contracts trade at 3.7x EV/NTM sales on lower-leverage balance sheets. Covers the six energized mining sites (1,471 MW); Massillon's 47 MW rebuild and Fox Creek are not added (post-halving NPV of new mining capacity ~zero or negative).
Same as DCF.
H1-26 G&A $58.9M x 2 = ~$118M/yr at 3x. R&D is left inside the mining multiple, because SEALMINER R&D supports the fleet. This closes the gap I flagged in round 3 (the SOTP had no corporate line).

bear.story: BTC retraces toward $60K into the 2028 halving and mining burns cash. Tydal project debt slips or the LCs are not put in place. A202's $98M/yr facility fee runs with no offtake, and Knoxville/Wenatchee sit idle. ~$2.4B of horizon net debt must be refinanced, including the 13% BIT loans, so equity is raised deeply below today's price. Contracted cash flows (Tydal, A201, A102) do not cover the debt, as the negative DCF shows.

base.story: Tydal is delivered by Mar-27 and funded with project debt priced near the 7-9% precedents. A102 and A201 bill from 2027, and A202 signs part of its capacity. The market keeps paying for HPC-lease and BTC optionality well above my ~$3.5 fundamental value, and ATM issuance at those prices is accretive to existing holders. Debt load, the halving and a 10-yr A202 fee cap the stock below today's price.

bull.story: A second hyperscale/AI lease on US power (Rockdale or Weathersfield), A202 fully contracted at A102-like pricing, BTC >$110K and SEALMINER sales. BTDR re-rates toward AI-contracted peers. Needs a lease and a BTC rally together.

thesis_break_reason: Kept at ~$4.00, although my fair value (~$3.5) is now just below it. Fair value here is a cash-flow anchor: the split-rate DCF is negative because ~$2.4B of horizon net debt exceeds contracted plus probability-weighted cash flows, and no sensible equity price falls that far while the option value is alive. At $4.00 the market cap (~$1.1B) is less than Tydal's split-rate value net of its remaining capex (~$1.2B), so the market would be giving nothing for A201/A102, mining or ~2 GW of uncontracted power. Getting there would most likely take an LC/Volta failure, a failed Tydal project financing or BIT-loan refinancing, or a deeply discounted equity raise to fund A201/A202 GPUs. BTC-beta volatility alone would not explain it.

key_uncertainties: Bitcoin price and hashprice: mining is still ~70% of 2027 revenue, and the April-2028 halving falls 6 months after the horizon

Funding: ~$2.4B of horizon net debt with the notes held as debt, plus ~$1.8B of A202 and ~$1.5B of Knoxville GPU capex if those sites sign; the mix of project debt, prepayments and ATM drives whether equity is diluted

Volta tenant credit: the ~$1.3B LCs are 'anticipated' and conditional, and the reported end-customer deal (~6 yrs) is shorter than the year-10 walk. The contracted-rate split adds ~$0.09B to Tydal only if the LCs are issued
A202: a 10-yr facility fee Bitdeer pays (amount not disclosed; I assume ~$98M/yr) against a 45% chance of offtake. Swing about -$0.4B to +$0.6B
Whether the A201 commitments turn into executed agreements (no customers, agreements or deposits disclosed)
GPU-cloud refresh economics: at 75% of today's per-MW price the refresh is roughly NPV-zero; a supply-long market (steeper path) takes the DCF to -$2.54

Uncontracted power (Rockdale, Weathersfield, Clarington, Molde): only ~$0.15B in the probability-weighted DCF vs $0.72B in the market-comps SOTP leg; this gap is most of the distance between the two methods besides corporate cost
reasoning: Round 4 makes two fixes and applies the round-3 supervisor corrections. (1) Sites: every one of the 20 inventory rows is now in the DCF exactly once (site_coverage). A202 is rebuilt the right way round: Bitdeer pays a 10-yr facility fee and has no offtake. That is now a 45%-probability GPU cloud with $1.8B of GPU capex, worth -$0.14B, against a +$0.25B colocation credit in round 3. A201 is weighted 85% on the signed >70% ($340M/yr). Knoxville, Wenatchee and Tydal P3 replace the generic pipeline cohort as probability-weighted builds, net of capex. Probability-weighted US HPC options are added, with Rockdale's lost mining deducted. The Tydal revenue row is made consistent with the single April-2027 phase. (2) Discounting: there is no contract-backed Bitdeer debt to anchor on, so I use TeraWulf's and Cipher's IG-backstopped HPC notes (7.1-7.75% at ~4% Treasuries, ~3.4pp spread) for an 8.75% rate on the LC-covered Tydal years 1-5. Unrated contract cash flows (Tydal years 6-10, the Malaysian offtakes) get 10.5%, and everything else 12%. The split adds only ~$0.11B (+$0.41/sh), because the LC slice is short and the GPU contracts are short. The larger moves come from the supervisor's corrections. Holding the 2032 notes as debt, dropping the ATM and fixing the capex bridge take horizon net debt from $1.345B to $2.38B, and shares from 330M to 275M. GPU capex falls to 1.6x revenue and refresh to roughly NPV-zero. DCF: $0.38 -> -$2.43 at a single rate, -$2.02 split. SOTP $6.95 -> $6.47 (Tydal and the AI book up, net debt up, corporate G&A line added). Blended fair value $3.50 (was $4.65). That matches the supervisor's corrected ~$3.5 for my model, so the fixes reconcile. The stock at $10.64 is pricing option value on BTC, a second lease and continued equity issuance at high prices. With 108% vol I don't expect that to close within 12 months. I shift the ladder ~6% lower in strike terms (median ~$8.4 from ~$8.9; P(>=spot) 0.39), trim the scenarios to $3.6/$8.5/$18 (33/45/22%) and keep the thesis break at $4.00. Research this round: 3 searches (TeraWulf notes, Cipher notes, Tydal financing; no Tydal financing found) and 1 failed FRED fetch. IREN's useful life is corrected to 5 years from the fact-check.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted cohorts at contract price for the term (A102 $160M/yr to end-2031; A201 committed 70% at $340M/yr x 85%; A101 ~$35M/yr to ~2029), prepayments deducted from contract cash over the term. Uncontracted capacity and post-contract tails as % of launch price by age 1-9: 100/70/52/45/40/35/31/27/24. Cash cost 20% of revenue + fixed power $0.8M/MW + facility fee $1.5M/MW (leased halls) or $0.3M/MW upkeep (owned), +3% of launch revenue for repairs after year 5. Refresh at the end of a 6-yr life at 1.6x first-year revenue (GB300) or $28M/MW (Rubin): 75% of today's per-MW price, 60% re-contracted for 5 yrs, 40% on the decay path (about NPV-zero at 12%); later refreshes NPV-zero.
gpu_life.note: Values are split-rate DCFs ex-issuance with notes as debt. GPU research applied in full to the Malaysian halls (A101, A102, A201, A202), the legacy fleet and the Knoxville/Wenatchee conversions. Tydal gets only the tenant-credit overlay (year-7 default). Mining is unaffected. Company lives corrected per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5. Supply-long steeper path -$2.54. The life choice moves the DCF ~$0.7/sh from 5 to 7 years. The bigger levers are horizon debt, the A202 fee and refresh pricing.

discounting.basis: 8.75% applies to cash flows backed by investment-grade credit: Tydal lease years 1-5, which the ~$1.3B of letters of credit arranged by JPM affiliates covers (sum of rent ~$1.24B). Bitdeer has no secured debt priced against a contract; its only priced secured debt is the related-party BIT loan at 13.0% against mining assets, which is not contract-backed. So the anchor is the closest precedent: TeraWulf's $3.2B 7.75% and Cipher's $1.4B 7.125% HPC project notes, both backed by a Google lease backstop. They carried ~3.4pp over a ~4% Treasury, and today's 10-yr is 5.29% (FRED), giving ~8.7%, rounded up for conditional LCs and completion risk. 10.5% applies to unrated contract cash flows: Tydal years 6-10 on Volta's credit alone, and the A101/A102/A201 GPU offtakes with undisclosed customers, short terms and >50% of capex prepaid. 12% WACC applies to Tydal years 11-16 (no-fee walk right), post-contract tails, refreshes, all pipeline, mining, corporate and terminal. The split adds ~$111M of EV (+$0.41/sh): Tydal +$88M, A201 +$17M, A102 +$6M.
